title: What is known about 1RB0RF_1LC1RA_0RD0LC_1LB1RE_---0RA_1RC1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_1LC1RA_0RD0LC_1LB1RE_---0RA_1RC1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is a long alternating stretch (10)^n holding a single marker 0, followed by a short, changing tail at the right end that behaves like a binary counter. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves no halt in the first 10,000 steps by the kernel alone and in the first 107 with native_decide; the C simulator finds no halt in the first 109 steps; an exact macro simulator (blocks of 12 cells) finds no halt in the first 1012 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 3,893 cells have been visited and 2,178 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/power
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.295). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.349).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>12</sup> steps
claims.text: An exact macro simulator (blocks of 12 cells) runs 1012 steps without a halt. The macro simulator cuts the tape into blocks of K cells, run-length codes them, and crosses a whole run at once when the head leaves it on the far side in the state it entered with; it agrees with the plain simulator tools/c/tmrun cell for cell.

claims.title: A marker counted in binary
claims.text: At the moments the head first reaches a new cell on the right, the tape is 0 (10)^x 0 (10)^y followed by a short tail; between consecutive such moments in one round, x grew by 64 (104 times), 32 (99), 128 (85), 16 (79), 8 (43), 256 (43), 4 (23) and a handful of other amounts in the first 108 steps, with 139 resets. Read as: one marker step per sweep, and a binary counter in the tail that gains a digit at powers of 2.

claims.title: The halting state, seen from the run
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>8</sup> steps state E was entered 58,016 times, always reading a 1 (E0 halts); 57,572 of those times the head was at least 7 cells from both ends of the tape.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. A marker 0 drifts through a long alternating sea one cell per sweep while a binary counter at the right end counts the sweeps; when the marker reaches the far end a reset sweep starts the next round, one cell wider.

facts.text: No halt in an exact macro simulator (blocks of 12 cells).
The marker moves 8, 16, …, 256 cells between right growths: a binary sweep counter.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
No halt in the C simulator; 3,893 cells visited.

sections.heading: What the machine does
html: Stop the machine whenever its head first reaches a new cell on the right. With a for 10 and c for 1110, the tape around step 9.65·107:

• step 96,383,862: 0 a^24 0 a^842 c a c a^6 c 1^2 B>0
  • step 96,424,357: 0 a^32 0 a^834 c a c a^6 c 1^3 A>0
  • step 96,504,199: 0 a^48 0 a^818 c a c a^6 c 1^5 A>0
  • step 96,659,277: 0 a^80 0 a^786 c a c a^6 c 1^7 A>0
  • step 96,951,003: 0 a^144 0 a^722 c a c a^6 c 1^9 A>0
  • step 97,460,729: 0 a^272 0 a^594 c a c a^6 c 1^11 A>0
  • step 98,185,271: 0 a^528 0 a^338 c a c a^6 c 1^13 A>0
  • step 98,543,083: C>0 1^1738 c 1^12 c … (the reset sweep)
  • step 98,684,671: 0 a^28 0 a^842 c a^9 1^2 c a^2 1^2 B>0

The left part is an alternating sea 0 a^x 0 a^y with x + y fixed within a round (866 here, then 870): one extra 0, the marker, sits after x copies of 10. The head shuttles between the marker and the right end: going left (states C and D) it turns the sea right of the marker into solid 1s, at the marker it moves the marker one cell on, and going right (state F) it turns the 1s back into 10s, for example 0 a^33 0 a^303 F>1^1058. At the right end each sweep adds one to a counter in the tail, and the tape grows on the right only when the counter gains a digit. So between right growths the marker moves 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 cells: in the first 108 steps the increments were 64 (104 times), 32 (99), 128 (85), 16 (79), 8 (43), 256 (43), 4 (23) and a handful of others, with 139 resets. The counter counts sweeps in binary.

When the marker reaches the right end of the sea, a long sweep (C>0 1^1738 …) resets it near the left end, the counter's tail is rewritten, and the sea is a little longer. A round of a sea of width w is about w sweeps of about w steps, and the sea grows a little per round: the width grows like the cube root of the step count.

sections.heading: Where a halt would have to come from
html: The halting transition is E reading a 0. E is entered only from D reading a 1 (1RE), so a halt needs D on a 1 with a 0 just right of it. In the first 108 steps E was entered 58,016 times, every time on a 1, and 57,572 of those times at least 7 cells from both ends of the tape.

D runs left through the sea during a sweep (0 a^647 D>0 1^371); the danger would be a configuration of the sea or the counter where D meets 1 0 in the wrong phase. Whether the counter's carries or the resets can ever produce one is open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.295). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.349).
After 109 steps the tape spans 3,893 cells (246 left of the start, 2,958 right), with a density of 1s of 0.559.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
